name: Paul
note: The apostle (in the traditional view), writing from prison and expecting to die, with a message for Timothy and requests for his friends.

name: Timothy
note: Paul's "beloved child," who has a gift received through Paul's laying on of hands (1:6), tears Paul remembers (1:4), and a task to continue.

name: Lois and Eunice
note: Timothy's grandmother and mother, in whom "sincere faith" lived first (1:5); Acts 16:1 says his mother was Jewish and a believer.

name: Onesiphorus
note: Who "often refreshed" Paul and was not ashamed of his chain, searching for him in Rome (1:16-18; 4:19).

name: Phygelus and Hermogenes
note: Named among those in Asia who "turned away" from Paul (1:15).

name: Hymenaeus and Philetus
note: Whose teaching "will consume like gangrene"; they said the resurrection "is already past" (2:17-18). A Hymenaeus was also named in 1 Timothy 1:20.

name: Opponents and false teachers
note: People who argue about words, hold "a form of godliness," and "oppose the truth" (2:14-26; 3:1-9; 4:3-4).

name: Jannes and Jambres
note: Names not found in the Old Testament; Jewish tradition gave them to the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses (3:8).

name: Demas
note: Who left Paul, "having loved this present world" (4:10); earlier named as a co-worker in Colossians 4:14 and Philemon 1:24.

name: Mark
note: Whom Timothy is to bring, "for he is useful to me for service" (4:11).

name: Alexander the coppersmith
note: Did Paul "much evil" and "greatly opposed our words" (4:14-15); whether he is the Alexander of 1 Timothy 1:20 is uncertain.

name: Prisca and Aquila
note: The couple Paul asks Timothy to greet (4:19).

name: Crescens, Titus, Carpus, Erastus, Trophimus, and others
note: Co-workers named as sent, left, or present (4:10-21), including Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, and Claudia, who send greetings.

name: Christ Jesus
note: Risen from the dead, descended from David (2:8); who "abolished death" (1:10) and will judge the living and the dead (4:1).
